variants.reconstruction:
%n [...] | enk[ī]du? | pâšu | [īpuša]
#note: See @bib{RN117@330}: “ii 1. The use of the sign KA×U for @i{pû} is a distinctive western phenomenon, occurring also at Boǧazköy, Ugarit and Amarna. References have been collected by @bib{RN649@186}.”
variants.intertext: The tablet is a fragment from the top right-hand corner from a tablet of two columns per side. The text of reverse comes from a passage in which Gilgamesh and Enkidu strengthen their resolve for the confrontation with Ḫumbaba in the Cedar Forest. This episode fell in SB Tablet V in the late epic. the key word is @i{mušḫalṣītum} in l. 8′ occurs in SB V 74. However, the text of the Emar fragment has little in common with the late edition (adapted from @bib{RN117@328–329}).

variants.reconstruction:
%n [enkīdu] | pâšu | īpuša | i[qabbi]
#note: See @bib{RN117@330}: “iii 3'. Now that the identification of obverse and reverse is secured and the fragment of text here identified as col. ii is no longer seen to be a continuation of the conversation introduced by this line, we are no longer obliged to understand Gilgameš as the subject. Reference to the late version indicates that there it is Enkidu who speaks of the @i{mušḫalṣītu} (SB V 74) and this must also be the case here. Given the limited space available on the tablet it seems that after @i{iqabbi} the scribe omitted the expected continuation, @i{issaqqara ana Gilgāmeš}.”
